summary.en: Pakistani security forces are again confronting Afghan Taliban infiltration along the Kurram border, arresting militants, destroying posts and killing attackers after cross-border fire. In Rawalakot security forces killed 18 protesters, including four children, during demonstrations over basic rights. A bus-truck collision on the Hazara Motorway killed eight and injured 30, while a shop roof collapse on Karachi’s Manghopir Road killed one person. The conflict produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker konfronterer igjen afghansk Taliban-infiltrasjon langs Kurram-grensen, arresterer militante, ødelegger poster og dreper angripere etter grensekryssende skyting. I Rawalakot drepte sikkerhetsstyrker 18 demonstranter, inkludert fire barn, under protester over grunnleggende rettigheter. En buss-lastebil-kollisjon på Hazara-motorveien drepte åtte og såret 30, mens et tak på en butikk i Manghopir-gate i Karachi kollapset og drepte én person. Konflikten førte til 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
